title: Lydia Festival Venue
subject: Civil Procedure
stem:
Source row: BarMatrix Q# 20606 is a federal diversity venue question with the official credited answer listing the accident district plus both defendants’ residence districts.

Final Christian variation

Lydia, a worship harpist domiciled in the Northern District of State G, was injured when a propane coffee cart exploded during a privately run Christian music festival in the Central District of State H. Lydia filed a federal action based on diversity against two individuals involved in setting up the cart. Peter, a stage electrician, is domiciled in the Eastern District of State J. Ruth, a carpenter who built the cart platform, is domiciled in the Western District of State J.

In which judicial districts would venue be proper for Lydia’s action?

---
call: In which judicial districts would venue be proper for Lydia's action?

choices.A: The Eastern District of State J and the Western District of State J.
choices.B: The Central District of State H.
choices.C: The Central District of State H, the Eastern District of State J, and the Western District of State J.
choices.D: The Northern District of State G and the Central District of State H.

rightExplanation:
C is correct. Gold Key: For ordinary federal civil actions, venue can be proper in a district where a substantial part of the events occurred, and also in a district where any defendant resides if all defendants reside in that same state. Silver Key: Treat the answer choices as bucket checklists: event bucket, defendant-residence bucket, and plaintiff-home lure.

The explosion occurred in the Central District of State H, so that district is a proper event venue. Peter and Ruth both reside in State J, though in different districts, so each district where one of them resides is also a proper defendant-residence venue. The complete list is therefore the Central District of State H, the Eastern District of State J, and the Western District of State J.

---

c3.label: CUT A
c3.text: Keeps the defendant-residence bucket but omits the event bucket. Anchor-assisted wrong-element cut.

c3.label: CUT B
c3.text: Keeps the event bucket but omits the defendant-residence bucket. Anchor-assisted wrong-element cut.

c3.label: CUT D
c3.text: Adds the plaintiff-home bucket. Anchor-assisted flat-misstatement cut.

c3.label: Residual
c3.text:
C. No CLASH or CALL needed after the anchor-assisted cuts.

---

studentScript: Venue buckets: event in State H, defendants in State J. Keep Central H, Eastern J, Western J. Do not add Northern G.

A.signal: It keeps defendant residence districts but drops the event district.
A.lawyer: Venue also lies where a substantial part of the events occurred.

B.signal: It keeps the accident district but drops both defendant-residence districts.
B.lawyer: Venue also lies in a district where any defendant resides when all defendants reside in that state.

C.signal: It includes the event district and both defendant-residence districts, with no plaintiff-home lure.
C.lawyer: This matches the event venue and same-state defendant-residence venue rules.

D.signal: It adds Lydia's home district, which the Gold Key marks as outside the ordinary venue buckets.
D.lawyer: The ordinary private-defendant venue rule does not make the plaintiff's home district proper merely because the plaintiff resides there.

goldKeys.statement: For ordinary federal civil actions, venue can sit in the event district or in a defendant-residence district when all defendants reside in that same state; the plaintiff's home is not a venue bucket.
goldKeys.trigger: The call asks which judicial districts are proper and gives accident location plus defendants from different districts of one state.

silverKeys.statement: Read list answers as bucket checklists: keep every valid bucket and reject any answer that adds a false bucket or omits a true one.
silverKeys.trigger: Choices mix event district, defendant districts, and plaintiff home district.
